subject: ela
intro: Analyze how structure advances an argument.

items.prompt:
How an author arranges the parts of a text is its:
A) structure
B) font
C) length

The position an author argues is the:
A) claim
B) title
C) rhyme

In a strong argument, claims and evidence should be:
A) logically sequenced
B) randomly scattered
C) left out

An argument presents strong evidence first, then answers objections, then restates the claim. This structure:
A) builds a persuasive, credible case
B) confuses the reader
C) hides the claim
items.answer: A) builds a persuasive, credible case

solution.answer: A) builds a persuasive, credible case

items.prompt:
Why place a COUNTERARGUMENT just before the conclusion?
A) to remove the reader's doubts right before the final claim
B) to start a new topic
C) to weaken the claim
items.answer: A) to remove the reader's doubts right before the final claim

solution.answer: A) to remove the reader's doubts right before the final claim

items.prompt:
A well-sequenced argument helps the reader by:
A) making it clear and easy to follow
B) hiding the point
C) adding confusion
items.answer: A) making it clear and easy to follow

steps: Logical sequence aids clarity. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) making it clear and easy to follow

items.prompt:
An author structures an essay as: claim, three reasons from weakest to STRONGEST, then conclusion. Ending on the strongest reason is effective because it:
A) leaves the reader with the most convincing point fresh in mind
B) buries the best point
C) has no effect
items.answer: A) leaves the reader with the most convincing point fresh in mind

solution.answer: A) leaves the reader with the most convincing point fresh in mind

items.prompt:
To analyze how STRUCTURE advances an argument, examine:
A) how the claim, reasons, and evidence are sequenced and how sections develop the points
B) only the word count
C) only the title
items.answer: A) how the claim, reasons, and evidence are sequenced and how sections develop the points

steps: Sequence + section function. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) how the claim, reasons, and evidence are sequenced and how sections develop the points
